Fixed release builds showing a DEV marker on the on-device updates splash and in the fb-im technician tool. Both treated FirstBaseBuildStatus in FirstBaseVersion.ps1 as a dev signal, but that is a checked-in constant rather than a build output, so every build inherited whatever value was committed. Dev status is now decided only by artifacts the builder stamps per build.

Dev/release detection is now one shared function (FirstBaseBuildIdentity.ps1) used by the WinPE banner, the WinPE deploy screen, the updates splash, the handoff splash and fb-im, replacing four separate implementations. It reads LW_VERSION.json devBuild first, then the .dev-build marker, and treats a missing or unreadable signal as release - a dev stick losing its tag is cosmetic, a release device claiming DEV is not.

TechInstall now stages LW_VERSION.json and the .dev-build marker to C:\Windows\Setup\FirstBase alongside the resolver, so the on-device surfaces have the same per-build evidence the WinPE surfaces already had. Previously neither reached the device, which is why the splash had nothing real to read. Payload 2320-winpe-ps-ui -> 2321-dev-marker-parity.

WinPE deploy terminal is now a PowerShell visual environment (Invoke-FbDeployUi.ps1). Instead of a scrolling echo progress bar, the console holds one repainted screen: branded header with the workflow and DEV tags, the full step plan with each step marked pending / active / done, a progress bar, a live detail line, and a launcher + scripts + elapsed footer. Failure and completion get their own full-screen treatment, with the last 10 log lines shown inline on a failure. Wired into all three deploy profiles (Updates, No Updates, WIN-INSTALL); the old echo bar is retained as an automatic fallback for a WinPE without PowerShell.

Handoff splash (FirstBaseHandoffSplash.ps1): after the final restart the technician now gets a screen stating the outcome - sealed and ready, hardware-gate failure, or a generic restart - which stays open until it is explicitly closed. It does not delay or block the restart itself, and it removes its own scheduled task and marker once dismissed.

Updates splash no longer renders a blank status area. Get-FbSplashStateVersionText was a stub returning an empty string, so the line under the header was always empty; it now reports pipeline phase, pass and version without exposing KB IDs or update titles. The status card also shows an explicit 'checking for updates' state instead of an empty panel before the first wu-status.json write, the loop's message field is bound again, and the dead WarningText lookup is resolved.

WinPE console no longer prints 'The system cannot find the path specified.' The WinPE log was opened under %TEMP% before wpeinit had run, with no stderr redirection; %TEMP% is now validated with an X:\ fallback and the log writes are redirected. The UEFI preflight also stopped echoing its status lines to the console, restoring the intended silent pre-banner phase.

Fixed a deploy bug that had been firing on every run: a for /f command string beginning with a double quote never executed, printing a syntax error and leaving MEDIADISK empty, which silently skipped the split-USB ESP disarm and the offline-disk step. Both call sites now use the capture-file diskpart pattern and log the resolved disk number. disksetup.cmd and TechInstall.cmd also agree on the payload root for their logs and operator flags. Runs from the stick, so it still works after the device has been scrubbed.

WinPE deploy banner now marks dev builds: a red DEV tag sits beside the [ Updates ] / [ No Updates ] workflow tag and the footer prints the launcher and script versions (red with the share versions alongside on a dev stick, grey on a release stick). FirstBase payload: made the 2305 seal-window splash teardown REVERSIBLE on a refused OOBE hand-off (follow-up to 2305). 2305 tore the splash down permanently the moment the seal window opened, which was correct for a committed seal but wrong when the STAGE 1 convergence gate REFUSES the hand-off and reboots for another UPDATE PASS: two persistent bits of state (the State\.splash-teardown marker + End/DISABLE'd splash tasks, and the .oobe-seal-window seal guard that halts Layer 2) kept the splash down forever after the first hand-off attempt, so no progress UI showed on the subsequent update passes. Fix (tag 2306): Invoke-WindowsUpdateLoop.ps1 adds Invoke-FbSplashSealTeardownRevert (a mirror of Invoke-FbSplashSealTeardown) called ONLY on the STAGE 1 residual-refusal branch (the sole exit that clears PendingSysprep=false and reboots for another pass), right before Invoke-FbReboot. It reverts the FULL seal-window state in order: (1) remove the seal guard .oobe-seal-window so Layer 2 (kill-OOBE) + Layer 4 operate again next boot (without this the splash would run but stay stuck behind OOBE - the original bug), (2) schtasks /Change /ENABLE the same five splash tasks 2305 disabled (UpdateSplash, SplashWatcher, UpdateSplashLayer4, UpdateSplashInteractive[Launch]) so the ONSTART watcher relaunches, (3) remove the cooperative State\.splash-teardown marker so Show-UpdateProgress.ps1 spins up and the watcher stops standing down. The COMMITTED / seal path is unchanged - it stays permanently torn down. Safe because the next hand-off attempt re-writes the seal guard + re-runs the teardown on entry (reversal is re-armed each attempt), and because Show-UpdateProgress.ps1 / FirstBaseSplashWatcher.ps1 already re-arm automatically once the marker + seal guard are gone (no change needed to those files). Seal-safety preserved: reversal happens only on the refused branch; STAGE 2 CBS-not-settled and sysprep-failure retries keep PendingSysprep=true and stay torn down (still sealing, no update passes); Invoke-FbPreSysprepScrub L1/L3/L4 reverts, loop re-arm, Bug U/B1 fences, overlay.mode, sysprep, and the deferred-sound/finalize chain are untouched. Payload rev 2305-splash-seal-teardown -> 2306-splash-seal-teardown-reversible; Invoke-WindowsUpdateLoop.ps1 1.0.6 -> 1.0.7. FirstBase payload: clean splash teardown at the OOBE-handoff seal window (complements 2304's pre-seal reclaim). Root cause: the seal-window guard (.oobe-seal-window, written when the loop enters Invoke-FbOobeHandoff) correctly halts Layer 2 so the splash can no longer take the foreground, but nothing told the splash to EXIT - so it lingered behind OOBE for the entire hand-off, including the STAGE 1 'refused; reboot for another pass' window (the exact boot the operator saw). The pre-sysprep scrub only tears the splash down later on the committed path (and defers it under OOBE-overlay mode), so it never covered the seal window. Fix (tag 2305): the moment the seal window opens, Invoke-WindowsUpdateLoop.ps1 now calls a new Invoke-FbSplashSealTeardown that (1) writes a cooperative State\.splash-teardown marker, (2) End+DISABLE the splash scheduled tasks (UpdateSplash, SplashWatcher, UpdateSplashLayer4, UpdateSplashInteractive[Launch]) so nothing relaunches it, and (3) force-kills lingering splash processes by command-line match. Show-UpdateProgress.ps1 closes + exits on the marker (bypassing the Updates-Done close guard, and refusing to spin up WPF if the marker is already present); FirstBaseSplashWatcher.ps1 stands down on the marker and never relaunches. Seal-safety preserved: the teardown ONLY stops the splash - it disables (does not delete) tasks, never touches the seal guard, overlay.mode, sysprep, the OOBE regeneration, or the deferred-sound / operator-finalize chain, and Invoke-FbPreSysprepScrub's layer reverts / re-arm / Bug U/B1 fences are unchanged. Layer 3 (splash-as-shell) guard: if the .splash-shell-mode marker is present the teardown stands down entirely so the scrub's ordered Shell=explorer.exe restore is what removes the shell (never leaves the session shell-less). FirstBase payload: 3rd-boot regression follow-up to the 2303 splash/OOBE activation fix, from two on-box bundles (machine SD00HN3R, payload=2303 confirmed running). Root cause: the ONLY primitive that reliably surfaces the splash is Layer 2 killing the OOBE host that holds the foreground - post-kill SetForegroundWindow returns True gle=0 every time, while the self-window minimize->restore reclaim (reclaim-2214b) fails every time (SetForegroundWindow False, no fresh error). Two failure modes made the splash sit behind OOBE: (1) the Layer 2 backoff throttled the kill to ~1 per 20s after only 3 kills, so during the WWAHost respawn storm the splash was hidden between kills; and (2) on the later boot the update loop reached the OOBE handoff and the seal-window guard correctly halted Layer 2 (protecting the real customer OOBE being regenerated at sysprep) - so WWAHost held the foreground uncontested. Fixes (tag 2304): (a) added SwitchToThisWindow (the Alt+Tab shell's own activation API, which the operator confirmed surfaces the splash) as a cheap first try in the self-activate path, before and after the minimize->restore; (b) raised the per-boot/per-proc kill ceiling from 3 to 30 so the proven kill+activate keeps firing through the respawn storm (the storm subsides within ~1 min once updates progress); (c) coupled the reclaim path to the proven kill+activate - when the self-window activation still cannot take the foreground from an OOBE-family host, it escalates to the seal-gated Layer 2 kill. All activation acts only on the splash's own window/input; the Layer 2 seal-window gate is unchanged, so nothing touches the real customer OOBE during the seal window (during seal the splash intentionally yields - suppressing OOBE there would hide the customer handoff). Payload rev 2303-splash-fg-activation -> 2304-splash-fg-spawn-reclaim; Show-UpdateProgress.ps1 1.0.4 -> 1.0.5. Requires rebuilding sticks; a stuck box can be dev-retested by dropping the updated Show-UpdateProgress.ps1 into C:\Windows\Setup\FirstBase\ and rebooting 3x to reproduce the 3rd-boot case (cfg already has FIRSTBASE_SPLASH_KILL_OOBE=1).

FirstBase payload: follow-up to the 2302 splash/OOBE fix after the on-box 1253 validation run (machine SD00HN3R). The 2302 diagnostics showed the picture had changed: the foreground LOCK is now cleared (fgLockTimeout=0ms, driven by the SetupComplete registry seed of ForegroundLockTimeout=0), yet SetForegroundWindow was still refused - the splash is topmost and Alt+Tab-activatable but cannot self-activate, because a background thread lacks SetForegroundWindow activation rights (AttachThreadInput to the WWAHost CoreWindow thread also fails). Three changes: (Fix 0) initialized the per-tick fglock state variable that was throwing every tick under StrictMode, and documented that SystemParametersInfo(SPI_SETFOREGROUNDLOCKTIMEOUT=0) returns ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER (gle=87) on Windows build 26100 regardless of marshaling (IntPtr/UIntPtr), flags, or value - it is cosmetic because the registry seed is what clears the lock; the gle logging is kept. (Fix 1) the foreground reclaim now fires a real Alt (VK_MENU) key tap instead of the inert VK_F15 - giving the activation the same user-input provenance the operator's working Alt+Tab uses - and, when SetForegroundWindow is still refused, performs a guarded self minimize->restore of the splash window plus a HWND_TOPMOST/BringWindowToTop re-assert, with post-attempt SetForegroundWindow + GetLastError logging under a new 2303 self-activate tag. (Fix 2) after a successful Layer 2 kill the splash now claims the foreground in the SAME tick (Alt tap + topmost re-assert + SetForegroundWindow, with the minimize->restore fallback) to beat the WWAHost respawn race, instead of waiting for the next ~1.5s UI refresh. All activation actions touch only the splash's own window and our own input (seal-safe); Layer 2's seal-window gate and 3-kills/20s backoff are unchanged. FirstBase payload: fixed the Audit-Mode update splash rendering but staying hidden behind the OOBE host (field report: machine SD00HN3R, Lenovo). Root cause from the runtime logs: Layer 1 fglock never lifts the foreground lock - SystemParametersInfo(SPI_SETFOREGROUNDLOCKTIMEOUT=0) returns ok=False and the effective ForegroundLockTimeout stays pinned at 2147483647ms (0x7FFFFFFF, set by the OOBE/CloudExperienceHost host), so every SetForegroundWindow and AttachThreadInput from the splash is rejected by the foreground lock. The splash is topmost but loses the foreground/z-order fight to WWAHost's Windows.UI.Core.CoreWindow; only real user input (Shift+F10 opening a console) satisfied the recent-input gate and released the pending foreground change. Three changes: (A) diagnostics - capture and log Marshal.GetLastWin32Error() after the SPI set and after the 2214b SetForegroundWindow so the exact denial code is recorded; (B) re-apply SPI_SETFOREGROUNDLOCKTIMEOUT=0 on every ~1.5s refresh tick (guarded on Layer 1 being enabled, fully wrapped, logs only on state-change) so an OOBE-re-forced lock keeps getting zeroed; (C) enabled Layer 2 (kill OOBE host when it holds the foreground) by default - it remains seal-window-gated and per-proc backoff-limited, so it is safe during the pre-seal audit window and never touches the real customer OOBE regenerated at sysprep. Payload rev 2301-splash-cfg-paren-fix -> 2302-splash-oobe-fg-reclaim; Show-UpdateProgress.ps1 1.0.2 -> 1.0.3; SetupComplete.cmd 1.0.3 -> 1.0.4. Requires rebuilding sticks for the baked-in Layer 2 default; a stuck box can be fixed in-place by editing C:\Windows\Setup\FirstBase\splash-suppression.cfg to FIRSTBASE_SPLASH_KILL_OOBE=1 and rebooting.

CRITICAL payload fix (blocked entire 4.1.4 audit pipeline, not just the splash): SetupComplete.cmd's 2300 Phase 0 block wrote splash-suppression.cfg with echo lines containing UNESCAPED parentheses (e.g. '(default 0):', '(2300).') INSIDE an if/else ( ... ) block. cmd treats the first bare ')' as the block terminator, so the script aborted with 'was unexpected at this time.' immediately after seeding Layer 1 fglock and BEFORE arming any scheduled tasks - so the SplashWatcher/UpdateSplash/WindowsUpdateLoop tasks were never created and the splash never fired (field report: machine SD00HN3R). The failure was deterministic and hardware-independent on every 4.1.4 stick. Fix: moved the cfg body into a flat :WRITE_SPLASH_SUPPRESS_CFG subroutine (outside any parenthesized block, where literal parens are safe) and reworded the else-branch log to drop its parens. Reproduced the abort and verified the fix parses/executes green in isolation. Payload rev 2300-oobe-splash-suppression-layers -> 2301-splash-cfg-paren-fix; SetupComplete.cmd 1.0.2 -> 1.0.3. Requires rebuilding sticks.

FIX (wim-split): the on-the-fly split fell over with a bogus 'DISM /Split-Image (install.wim) failed (exit ):' even though DISM reported 'The operation completed successfully'. In the -Progress (async) path added in 5.2.74, DISM is launched via Start-Process -PassThru; the process handle was not retained, so .NET released it on exit and $proc.ExitCode came back $null -> $null -ne 0 was misread as a failure and aborted the build (disk 3). Fix: reference $proc.Handle immediately after launch (retains the handle so ExitCode survives), call WaitForExit() before reading it, and guard the failure check with $null -ne $exit so a still-null code falls through to the existing install.swm existence/chunk validation instead of false-failing. Applied to both the install.wim and install.esd split branches in lib\Split-LWImage.ps1.

FIX (pre-split fast-copy never engaged - root cause): the builder's Emit JSON-event helper used 'Write-Output', which places every event on the PowerShell success (pipeline) stream. Because Get-LWPreSplitSet calls EmitLog internally and its return value is captured ($resolvedSet = Get-LWPreSplitSet ...), the emitted 'presplit: MATCH ...' JSON line was RETURNED alongside the staged-set path. $PreSplitSetDir thus became an array of [matchJson, setDir] that collapsed into a '{...MATCH json...} \\WIN-HQ5JDEACV3S\...\<imageVersion>' string when marshalled into each per-disk Start-Job, so the worker's Test-Path failed and every disk fell back to the on-the-fly dism /Split-Image despite a valid, matching set on the share. Emit now writes via [Console]::Out.WriteLine, which reaches the same stdout main.js parses but never enters the pipeline - so no function's return value can be polluted again. The per-disk worker's J emitter is intentionally left on Write-Output (its output is harvested by Receive-Job and must stay on the job output stream). Verified: a full ISO-mode Single-layout build now resolves a clean set path and enters the 'wim-presplit' fast-copy phase instead of 'wim-split'. Launcher/app version bumped 5.2.72 -> 5.2.73.

Diagnostics (pre-split fast-copy): the per-disk worker's on-the-fly-split fallback log line no longer reads the ambiguous 'presplit: no matching staged set for this ISO' in every case. It now distinguishes (a) an EMPTY set dir - the MAIN-THREAD detector Get-LWPreSplitSet found no valid/matching set, and the authoritative reason is the disk 0 'presplit:' line - from (b) a resolved-but-unreadable set dir, meaning detection matched on the main thread but the worker runspace could not reach the share path. This removes the confusion where the worker's echo looked like the detection verdict. No behavior change to detection or splitting. Verified against the live share that Get-LWPreSplitSet returns MATCH for a correctly-uploaded set, so a fresh full build (Local Build Mode off) fast-copies install*.swm. Added staged pre-split install.wim (Option A): a new one-shot producer (Stage-PreSplitImage.ps1) mounts a source ISO and splits sources\install.wim (or exports+splits install.esd) into a versioned install*.swm set on the share at Remote\Staging\PreSplit\<ARCH>\<imageVersion>\ with a presplit-manifest.json (schema 1: source-ISO identity, per-chunk sizes, optional -DeepHash sha256) and a 'current' marker. The USB builder now detects a valid, matching set for the ISO it is about to build from (Get-LWPreSplitSet: identity match on isoName+size+lastWriteUtc+imageVersion, mandatory per-chunk size validation, optional sha256 behind -VerifyPreSplitHash) and, in ISO-mode Single-layout builds, FAST-COPIES the already-split install*.swm straight from the share to the USB (new 'wim-presplit' phase) instead of running dism /Split-Image on every build. The split body was refactored into a shared dot-sourced helper (lib\Split-LWImage.ps1, Split-LWImageForFat32) used by BOTH the producer and the builder fallback, so a staged set is byte-identical to an on-the-fly split (same /FileSize:3800, same /CheckIntegrity, same ESD-export path, same chunk naming). A missing / mismatched / corrupt / unreadable set is NEVER fatal: the builder logs the reason and automatically falls back to the exact on-the-fly split used before this feature (Secure Boot loaders and boot.wim still come verbatim from the ISO - Option A). Get-StagingVersion now also reports preSplitAvailable / preSplitMatchesIso / preSplitImageVersion for the current arch's newest ISO. Fixed a Microsoft/Surface-only stall where the device 'was completed, settings closed, but did not scrub and shutdown to exit sysprep' (dump 0F000QG23233FB-0621-Microsoft, CPS-00QG23233FB). Confirmed the operator Settings gate WORKED on Surface: it acquired the live ApplicationFrameWindow hosting SystemSettings (hwnd=131880, hostsSettings=True) and correctly detected the operator close, starting its 6s close-grace at 06:14:03 - so this is NOT a strict-liveness/DWM-cloak/host-mapping detection bug. Root cause: the gate SCRIPT process (FirstBaseOpenSettingsAndFinish.ps1, PID 3120) then VANISHED mid-grace BEFORE it could conclude window-closed and write C:\ProgramData\FirstBase\.operator-settings-closed (no .NET/WER crash was logged; a Surface Kernel-Power 'power source change' fired at 06:14:07 inside the grace window - most consistent with an external interactive-session/power teardown on Surface hardware). The .operator-settings-gate-active marker was left present and the closed-marker was never written, so the SYSTEM loop's Invoke-FbOperatorSettingsGateInSession close-wait (which had already 'seen' SystemSettings) sat the FULL CloseTimeoutSec=2100s (35-min) backstop; the operator gave up at ~10 min. The chain would have self-recovered at ~06:45 but that is an unacceptable no-feedback hang.

Fix (Invoke-WindowsUpdateLoop.ps1 v1.0.9->1.0.10, function Invoke-FbOperatorSettingsGateInSession): the SYSTEM loop now watches the gate script's own process (Get-CimInstance Win32_Process for powershell.exe whose CommandLine contains FirstBaseOpenSettingsAndFinish.ps1 + -GateOnly). Once the gate process has been positively observed alive, if it disappears with no closed-marker the loop waits only a short 30s gate-death grace (re-checking the marker for a flush race) and then proceeds to the inline scrub/seal/sysprep, instead of waiting the full 35-min backstop. This is hardware-agnostic and directly fixes the reported symptom on ANY device whose gate process is torn down after the operator closes Settings.

Invariants preserved: the death detection keys on OUR gate SCRIPT process ending, NEVER on SystemSettings.exe (which merely suspends on a normal close), so the 5.0.40 anti-premature-close property is NOT regressed. The 5.0.41 strict-liveness / anti-zombie-frame close-detection inside the still-running gate is untouched. The detection only ARMS after the gate process is seen alive (a launch/startup race cannot false-trigger it) and treats a failed process query as 'assume alive' (falls through to the existing bounded CloseTimeoutSec backstop, never a false death). The 5.0.42 final-ship reaper and Option B (Administrator-session inline scrub, sysprep /oobe /shutdown last, no /r /fw) are unchanged.

Note on the remaining open question: the exact trigger that terminated the gate process on Surface is not definitively logged (no WER entry). Close-detection is now STRICT-liveness based (FirstBaseOpenSettingsAndFinish.ps1, FbSettingsWin32). New IsSettingsWindowLive(hwnd) tests the tracked handle each tick; new FindLiveSettingsWindow() finds a genuinely-live frame with NO title/any-frame fallback (those matched leftovers). DwmGetWindowAttribute(DWMWA_CLOAKED) is the key discriminator that separates an open window from a suspended/closed zombie frame

Re-acquire is no longer eager: when the tracked handle stops being live, the gate starts a bounded close-grace (WindowCloseGraceSec=6s) and only re-acquires if a DIFFERENT genuinely live+visible+uncloaked Settings window reappears within that grace (real re-host/navigation); if no live Settings window exists anywhere for the full grace, it concludes reason=window-closed. This recognizes a real close within ~6s yet cannot false-positive early (a genuinely open window is live every tick). Each decision logs a dump-capturable DescribeWindow() breakdown (isWindow/visible/cloaked/class/hostsSettings)

On conclude-closed the gate removes .operator-settings-gate-active and writes the closed-marker (reason=window-closed); the SYSTEM loop then proceeds to the inline scrub -> .pipeline-completed/.firstbase-sealed -> sysprep /oobe /shutdown. Fixed the Single-layout LoneWolf USB still booting the Windows Boot Manager and then silently resetting before WinPE prints anything (no deployment, no logs) even after the 5.0.29 {bootmgr} device=boot fix. Confirmed by dumping the fresh stick's BCD (5.0.29 changes were present and boot.sdi/boot.wim were correct) and diffing it against the stock ISO UEFI BCD

The Single-layout build now ships the ISO's own \efi\microsoft\boot\BCD verbatim (copied from the mounted ISO, BIOS \boot\BCD refreshed too) instead of hand-authoring one - exactly what stock removable Windows install media and the proven Build-UsbStick.ps1 do. That store boots the RAM disk via 'ramdisk=[boot]\sources\boot.wim' with {bootmgr} carrying NO device element, so [boot] resolves to the USB the boot manager was actually loaded from (safe on machines that already have Windows - no 'locate', no explicit partition) and it carries every element winload expects. The store's timeout is set to 0 and the boot menu suppressed so the technician is not left on a countdown; all other stock elements are preserved. Fixed the Single-layout LoneWolf USB booting into WinPE with no terminal output and then silently exiting/resetting without starting deployment (no FirstBase-UsbLogs written). Root cause: the freshly rebuilt WinPE BCD set the Windows Boot Manager device to 'locate=\EFI\Microsoft\Boot\bootmgfw.efi', which searches EVERY partition for that loader and anchors the boot device to the first match. On any QA machine that already has Windows installed, the internal disk's ESP also contains \EFI\Microsoft\Boot\bootmgfw.efi, so 'locate' resolved [boot] to the internal ESP; the ramdisk device 'ramdisk=[boot]\sources\boot.wim' then pointed at a partition with no boot.wim, the RAM disk could not be resolved, and WinPE never started. The {bootmgr} device is now 'boot' (the volume the boot manager was actually loaded from = the USB), which is unambiguous and matches stock Windows install media and the proven Build-UsbStick.ps1. The custom WinPE (winpeshl.ini + startnet.cmd + PowerShell OCs, verified present in both boot.wim indexes) now actually runs on boot, prints its banner, locates Deploy\TechInstall.cmd on the USB, and starts the image apply with visible progress. No {fwbootmgr} firmware-boot-order logic was reintroduced and Secure Boot handling is unchanged

Because the USB no longer carries an EFI System Partition GUID, only the internal disk's ESP exists after bcdboot, so bcdedit {fwbootmgr} can disambiguate cleanly - matching the proven local Build-UsbStick.ps1 default. The legacy Split (FAT32 ESP + NTFS data) layout is retained behind -Layout Split as a fallback for firmware that requires an ESP GUID

Single layout splits install.wim into install.swm chunks (DISM /Split-Image /FileSize:3800) so the >4 GB image fits the FAT32 4 GB per-file limit; the monolithic install.wim is never written to the FAT32 volume. The deploy side already applies from install*.swm via SWMFile when install.wim is absent (TechInstall.cmd + Invoke-FirstBaseDismApply.ps1), so no image is lost

Secure Boot is preserved: the Microsoft-signed loaders (\EFI\Boot\bootx64.efi removable-media fallback and \EFI\Microsoft\Boot\bootmgfw.efi) are copied byte-for-byte from the mounted ISO and never re-generated or re-signed; a build-time check now verifies both signed loaders are present on the volume and fails the build loudly if bootx64.efi is missing. Removed the unintended \boot\ folder (BIOS-only boot files - bcd, boot.sdi, bootfix.bin, bootsect.exe, memtest.exe, fonts) from the USB data partition root: the ISO-mode per-disk copy added in 5.0.18/5.0.19 robocopied the entire mounted ISO root with no exclusions; it now excludes \boot\, which is not needed for a UEFI-only deployment and was never referenced from the data partition

Fixed DISM apply progress showing nothing for the whole ~4 minute run and then jumping to 100% on a new line: without /Progress, DISM's /LogPath file never contains a percentage at all (only Info-level lifecycle lines), so the log-tail regex had nothing to match and the percent stayed pinned at 0% the entire time; live percent is now estimated from apply-drive disk usage (WIM uncompressed size read once via 'dism /Get-ImageInfo', free space polled every second via System.IO.DriveInfo - no process I/O redirection and no directory recursion, so no deadlock or performance risk), falling back to elapsed time + spinner only if either signal is unavailable. Also removed a stray unconditional blank-line write between the last live progress update and the final line, which was preventing the same-line overwrite on completion

Fixed DISM apply hanging forever right after the DISM command line was logged, with no progress and no exit code: the wrapper redirected both DISM stdout and stderr and drained them with a Peek()-gated ReadLine loop, but .NET's StreamReader.Peek() permanently latches non-blocking after the first partial pipe read (the documented _isBlocked behavior), so the loop silently stopped reading stdout after the first small burst; DISM's continuous /Progress output then filled the OS pipe buffer and DISM blocked forever on its own write with nothing left to drain it. Removed /Progress entirely and disabled stdout/stderr redirection so DISM inherits the console directly and cannot deadlock; live progress is now sourced purely from polling process exit state once a second and tailing the DISM /LogPath log file

Fixed startnet-inject failing on boot.wim index 2 with DISM error 0xc1420127 ('already mounted for read/write access'): a stale or not-yet-released mount on the WIM is now cleared before every mount attempt, /Mount-Image retries up to 3 times with a 2s backoff, and the code waits for /Unmount-Image /Commit's file lock to actually release before moving to the next index (both the per-disk worker and the cache-level Invoke-StartnetInjection)

Fixed ISO-mode per-disk WinPE DISM injection failing immediately on boot.wim index 1 with 'The term if is not recognized': inline if subexpression passed as a Start-Job function argument is not re-parsed correctly in the child runspace; progress percent is now assigned to a variable first (matching cache-level Invoke-StartnetInjection)

Fixed ISO-mode USB sticks booting to the Windows Setup language-selection screen instead of custom WinPE: per-disk DISM injection is no longer skipped by a stale ESP-cache sentinel, ReadOnly is cleared on ISO-sourced boot.wim before mount, and any injection failure in ISO mode aborts the disk build

Fixed DISM error 183 (Cannot create a file when that file already exists) on repeat deploys: the Windows target partition is now checked for stale content immediately before DISM apply and quick-formatted NTFS if a prior interrupted apply left files behind, preventing WinSxS collisions

Fixed the PowerShell DISM wrapper exiting with code 2 immediately in WinPE PowerShell 5.1: replaced the async BeginOutputReadLine and add_OutputDataReceived event pattern with synchronous log-file polling every 1 second, which is reliable in WinPE's restricted runspace where the event infrastructure can throw a terminating exception

Suppressed residual path-not-found console noise in disksetup.cmd: the USB log directory path is only committed when the directory was successfully created, and the pre-wipe annotation file is only written when the target directory is confirmed present

Fixed a persistent USB boot loop on hardware where the FAT32 ESP partition has no drive letter: the ESP is now disarmed by selecting it directly as Disk N Partition 1 via diskpart (bypassing the WinPE removable-media volume restriction that blocks letter assignment), assigning a temporary letter T:, removing bootx64.efi, and cleaning up the letter; this replaces the previous A-Z volume scan which never found the un-lettered ESP

Fixed a repeated re-imaging loop on hardware where the firmware boot store is inaccessible: the USB disarm now scans all already-lettered volumes for the FAT32 ESP signature using PowerShell Test-Path (bypassing the HIDDEN+SYSTEM attribute blindspot in cmd IF EXIST), so the EFI boot files are reliably removed even when the disk-number lookup fails; clears file attributes with attrib before each move and falls back to PowerShell Move-Item/Remove-Item if move fails
